clue.text: Article of clothing found in river I fish

parts.note: the Cam is the river flowing through Cambridge
a sole is a flatfish

explanation.surface: Someone fishing in a river hooks a garment instead of a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' is only a link: the pieces sit side by side, not one inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A camisole is a light sleeveless undergarment for the upper body, so a piece of apparel.

clue.text: Successfully manage work in church

indicators.note: in says the word for work is placed inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Someone handles a job in a church well.
explanation.definitionFit: To cope is to deal effectively with something difficult.

clue.text: Slander about a girl poet led up the garden path?

definitions.text: girl poet led up the garden path?

indicators.note: about means the word for slander goes around the next piece

parts.note: to throw mud is to slander, so mud means defamation

explanation.surface: Gossip about a young woman deceived by a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'led up the garden path' suggests being deceived; it alludes to Tennyson's poem in which the speaker begs 'Come into the garden, Maud'.
explanation.definitionFit: Maud is the girl Tennyson's speaker invites into the garden in his poem of that name.

clue.text: Cleric abused converted prisoner

indicators.note: converted means the letters of the word abused are changed into a new form

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner

explanation.surface: A clergyman ill-treated a prisoner who had found religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abused' looks like the anagram signal, but it is the fodder; 'converted' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A subdeacon is a cleric in minor orders ranking below a deacon.

clue.text: Short in one suit? That's not serious

parts.note: light means short, as in a measure that is light or under weight
hearted, as if holding hearts, one of the four card suits

explanation.surface: Someone is lacking in a suit of clothes, and it is no grave matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' suggests clothing but means the card suit hearts.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighthearted means cheerful and carefree, not grave or solemn.

clue.text: Obstructed, making confounded noise

indicators.note: making a noise like a word means the clue word is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: confounded, as a mild curse, means damned

explanation.surface: Someone blocked in their way lets out a curse.
explanation.definitionFit: A river that is blocked by a barrier has been held back or obstructed.

clue.text: A desire or aspiration

parts.note: an itch is a restless longing

explanation.surface: A wish or ambition is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aspiration' means ambition on the surface, but here it is the breathed sound of the letter H, whose name is spelt this way.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the letter H, which marks the aspirate or breathed sound in speech.

clue.text: Very old man displaying a lot of bottle

definitions.meaning: the Biblical patriarch said to have lived 969 years
a large wine bottle holding eight standard bottles

explanation.definitionFit: Methuselah is the longest-lived man of Genesis and also a very large champagne bottle.

clue.text: Tasteful record making money — no end of mazuma

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: no says the following letter is dropped from the word for making money

parts.note: earning is making money

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of the word mazuma

explanation.surface: A stylish record earns money, with the cash missing its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: Mazuma is slang for money; only its final A is used, removed from EARNING.
explanation.definitionFit: A discerning person shows good judgement and refined taste.

clue.text: After prize, shoot round in the lead

indicators.note: 'After prize' says the next pieces follow the word for prize in the answer

parts.note: a plum is a prize job or reward
to bag game is to shoot it
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A competitor wins an award, then shoots a round that puts them ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the lead' reads as being ahead in a contest; here 'the lead' is the metal-like substance, black lead or graphite.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumbago is an old name for graphite, which was long called black lead.

clue.text: Position of volunteers initially trained in South America

indicators.note: the volunteers and the trained initial are placed in the middle of the South and America pieces

parts.note: US is short for the United States of America
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: initially means take only the first letter of the word trained

explanation.surface: A question about where volunteers trained in South America stand.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is one's rank or standing, one's position in a hierarchy.

clue.text: Indiscreet peacekeepers face movement to limit certificate

indicators.note: to limit means this piece is put at the boundary, the end, of the certificate

parts.note: UN peacekeeping forces of the United Nations
a diploma is a certificate of qualification
a tic is an involuntary twitch, often of the face

explanation.surface: Peacekeepers confront a protest group about a document.
explanation.definitionFit: Undiplomatic means tactless, lacking discretion in dealing with people.

clue.text: Friends gather here, having satisfying game of bingo

parts.note: satisfying a demand is meeting it
house, or housey-housey, is an old British name for bingo

explanation.surface: People enjoy a pleasing round of bingo together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friends' with a capital F hides the Religious Society of Friends, the Quakers, whose place of worship is so named.
explanation.definitionFit: Quakers, formally the Society of Friends, worship in a building of this name.

clue.text: Novel is mislaid, unfortunately, before beginning to read

indicators.note: before puts the rearranged letters in front of the next piece
unfortunately signals the letters have come to grief and fallen into a new order
beginning to means take the first letter of the word read

explanation.surface: A novel has been lost just before someone was going to start reading it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book; it is the adjective meaning new or different.
explanation.definitionFit: Something novel is unlike anything before, different or unlike.

clue.text: Impractical, lacking skill to frame painting, perhaps

indicators.note: to frame means the first piece surrounds the second like a picture frame

parts.note: unable means lacking the ability
a painting is an example of a work of art

explanation.surface: An unskilled person can't manage to frame a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An unworkable plan cannot be put into practice; it is not feasible.

clue.text: Like a particle in one version of Greek

definitions.meaning: describing an electrically charged atom or molecule
the dialect of ancient Greek spoken in Ionia

explanation.definitionFit: Ionic means relating to charged atoms, and is also the dialect of Ionia in ancient Greece.

clue.text: Sort of pie and preserve taken by a Northern gourmet

indicators.note: a sort of pie is a rearranged version of the word pie

parts.note: to cure meat or fish is to preserve it

explanation.surface: A northern food lover eats a pie and some preserve.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicurean is a lover of fine food and drink, a person of refined taste.

clue.text: Say more than anyone else? That's the limit!

parts.note: to utter is to say
most means the greatest amount, more than any other

explanation.surface: Someone talks more than everyone, and it is exasperating.
explanation.definitionFit: The uttermost is the furthest extreme, the utmost point.

clue.text: The rogue cruel dons treated badly

indicators.note: letters treated badly are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: University teachers are mistreated by some villain.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoundrel is a dishonest, unprincipled person, a villain.

clue.text: Work out the following

definitions.meaning: to exercise or drill, as an athlete does
a retinue or procession of followers behind someone

explanation.definitionFit: To train is to exercise for fitness; a train is also the retinue following a dignitary.

clue.text: Sign with thumbprint, but achieve distinction?

definitions.meaning: to sign a document with a cross or print instead of a signature
to become successful and well known

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means leaving a print or cross as a signature, and also becoming famous or influential.

clue.text: Like eggs guzzled without hesitation

indicators.note: without means the hesitation sound is taken out of the word for guzzled

parts.note: to guzzle is to overeat, so guzzled means overate
er is the sound of hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: Eggs were wolfed down without pause.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovate means egg-shaped, from the Latin word for an egg.

clue.text: Profusely growing up? Not in wood, by the sound of it

definitions.text: Not in wood, by the sound of it

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: rank vegetation grows thickly and luxuriantly

explanation.surface: Something thriving lushly upward is not found in a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a sound pun: 'Not in wood' is heard as a knot in wood, which is what this word means.
explanation.definitionFit: A knar is a knot or gnarl on a tree trunk or in timber.

clue.text: Instrument used in masterly recital

indicators.note: used in says the answer is found inside the run of the next words

explanation.surface: A musical instrument features in a masterful performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyre is an ancient stringed instrument, a small harp.

clue.text: African politician reversed negative vote

parts.note: Lib is short for a Liberal politician

indicators.note: reversed says the word for a negative vote is read backwards

parts.note: nay is a vote against

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician changes their mind and votes against.
explanation.definitionFit: A Libyan is a native of Libya, a country in North Africa.

clue.text: Yatter on terribly as a lawyer

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are badly arranged and must be reordered

explanation.surface: A lawyer chatters on dreadfully.
explanation.walkthrough: To yatter is British slang for to chatter idly.
explanation.definitionFit: An attorney is a legal representative, a lawyer especially in the US.

clue.text: Advert recruiting English midshipman

indicators.note: recruiting means the first piece takes the second one in, enrolling it inside

parts.note: to advert to something is to refer to it

explanation.surface: An advertisement is used to recruit an English naval officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advert' looks like the noun for a commercial, but it is the verb meaning to allude.
explanation.definitionFit: Reefer was old naval slang for a midshipman, who had to reef sails.

clue.text: Second bed delivered unharmed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
delivered from captivity means set free

explanation.surface: A second bed is brought round safely.
explanation.definitionFit: To get off scot-free is to escape without punishment or injury.
